evidence.observation: The control reconciles 56 post-like variants minus two explicitly described render artifacts to 54 retained posts, records two terminal traversals with an exact fingerprint match, and reconciles all 54 publisher rows; the absence of non-identifying traversal digests limits independent recomputation and keeps this at 3.

The corpus, five-row Content Library, URL inventory, attributed memory, selected posts, and destination sources each identify review depth, support, and non-support; the Content Library is explicitly an incomplete subset rather than a historical control.

Seven separate claims distinguish population size, publisher metadata, attributed management, community routing, civic routing, engagement snapshots, and posted-URL routing instead of combining them into a single role or impact claim.

Every WOW List Facebook claim resolves to declared source IDs: population uses the private corpus plus Content Library boundary, management uses memory plus publisher metadata, and thematic claims use the corpus with selected close-read public posts.

All seven claims remain internal-only with no active projection; population and metrics are unused, publisher and thematic claims are candidates, and the broader management claim remains use-with-care.

The dossier situates the corpus within WOW List's community-calendar, cultural-space, mutual-aid, movement, and civic-routing work while treating selected posts as examples and destination records as separately reviewed research nodes.

The population inquiry is partially recovered and excludes deleted, unpublished, migration-omitted, and unavailable history; Jamie's management recollection remains attributed pending account or collaborator evidence, and mutable metrics and URLs are not promoted into attendance, endorsement, or impact.

The record-level corpus and URL inventory remain private behind protected opaque locator IDs with no filesystem, canonical, archive, or asset URL, while only aggregates and selected public sources enter the repository.
